evals.name: classify-and-report
evals.prompt: Review the skill in evals/fixtures/changelog-checker/ and tell me which of its workflow steps should be delegated to scripts. Don't change anything yet.
evals.expected_output: Rendered classification table: steps 1/2/3/5 SCRIPT with concrete proposed interfaces, step 6 HYBRID, steps 4 and 7 CLAUDE (7 despite containing the word 'verify'). Nothing written into the fixture; flow stops at the gate or explicitly notes changes await user selection.

assertions.text: output contains a per-step table with SCRIPT/CLAUDE/HYBRID classes and proposed script interfaces for SCRIPT/HYBRID rows
no new files or directories are created inside evals/fixtures/changelog-checker/
step 2 (version-header check) is classified SCRIPT with a concrete argv/exit-code interface
step 6 (category tags + Misc re-homing) is classified HYBRID
step 7 (verify entries clearly written) is classified CLAUDE despite the 'verify' verb
step 4 (release narrative) is classified CLAUDE

evals.name: apply-and-smoke-test
evals.prompt: Review the skill in evals/fixtures/changelog-checker/ for steps to delegate to scripts, apply all the delegations you find, and verify the generated scripts work.
evals.expected_output: Scripts written into changelog-checker/scripts/ for steps 1/2/3/5 (and the mechanical half of 6), each with --help support. Manifest includes bad_data_invocations; the header-check script flags v1.2.0.md. SKILL.md rewritten only after smoke test passes; steps 4 and 7 stay prose; step 6 keeps its judgment sentence.

assertions.text: changelog-checker/scripts/ contains at least 3 Python scripts and each supports --help
the rewritten SKILL.md invokes each generated script by exact command line
a smoke-test PASS result is reported before the SKILL.md rewrite is shown
the header-check script, run against changelogs/, flags v1.2.0.md and exits nonzero
step 4 (release narrative) remains a prose instruction with no script
step 6's judgment about re-homing Misc entries remains prose

evals.name: nothing-to-delegate
evals.prompt: Which parts of the skill in evals/fixtures/well-delegated/ should be scripts?
evals.expected_output: Report acknowledging scripts/check.py as already delegated (mentioned in body, argparse, working --help), classifying the remaining judgment steps CLAUDE, and recommending no new scripts.

assertions.text: no new files are written into evals/fixtures/well-delegated/
scripts/check.py is acknowledged as already delegated
the judgment steps (audience-fit decision, explanations) are classified CLAUDE, not forced into scripts

evals.name: partial-selection
evals.prompt: Review evals/fixtures/changelog-checker/ for delegable steps, but apply only the delegations for steps 1 and 3. Leave everything else untouched.
evals.expected_output: Exactly two scripts generated (file listing, category counting), both smoke-tested. Step 2's prose is byte-identical to before; the SKILL.md diff touches only steps 1 and 3.

assertions.text: exactly two generated scripts exist in changelog-checker/scripts/
the SKILL.md rewrite touches only steps 1 and 3; step 2's text is unchanged
both generated scripts pass the smoke test before the rewrite

evals.name: prose-only-headings
evals.prompt: Which parts of the skill in evals/fixtures/prose-only-reviewer/ should be scripts? Don't change anything yet.
evals.expected_output: Report covering all three heading-fallback anchors: link collection and target resolution SCRIPT with concrete interfaces, the fix-order decision CLAUDE. The skill does not report 'nothing to delegate' just because the target has no numbered steps.

assertions.text: the report contains a row for every anchor; the flow does not stop at '0 steps extracted'
no new files are written into evals/fixtures/prose-only-reviewer/
'Collect the link inventory' and 'Resolve each target' are classified SCRIPT with concrete argv/exit-code interfaces
'Decide what to fix now' is classified CLAUDE, since the deadline trade-off varies by run

evals.name: agent-tool-steps
evals.prompt: I want my research-brief-writer skill to stop re-deriving the same busywork on every run. Which of its steps should become scripts? The skill is at evals/fixtures/research-brief-writer/. Report only for now, don't change anything.
evals.expected_output: Report covering all 7 steps. Steps 1, 4, 7 SCRIPT with concrete interfaces. Step 2 (WebFetch), step 3 (AskUserQuestion) and step 5 (notion MCP) are never pure SCRIPT: a script may prepare input or digest output, but the tool call itself stays in the step. Step 6 keeps its prose-writing core. Nothing written into the target.

assertions.text: the report contains a row for every one of the 7 workflow steps, each with a class
no new files or directories are created inside the target skill folder
step 2 (WebFetch the top source) is NOT classified pure SCRIPT, and no proposed script reimplements the fetch with curl, requests, or urllib
step 5 (notion MCP page lookup and append) is NOT classified pure SCRIPT
step 3 (AskUserQuestion which sources to keep) is NOT classified pure SCRIPT
steps 1 (dedupe and slugify topics), 4 (word counts and thin-source flags) and 7 (render sorted index table) are classified SCRIPT with concrete argv/exit-code interfaces
step 6 (write the 200-word brief in the house voice) keeps its prose-writing core with Claude

evals.name: name-collision
evals.prompt: Scriptify the docs-linter skill at evals/fixtures/docs-linter/ — find the steps worth delegating and apply all of them.
evals.expected_output: The natural script name for step 2 is check_headings.py, which already exists in the target and does something unrelated (image alt text). The run must surface the collision to the user or pick a different name. The existing file stays byte-identical. Steps 1, 2, 3 get scripts; step 4 (which files matter this sprint) stays prose.

assertions.text: the pre-existing scripts/check_headings.py is byte-identical to its baseline copy (sha256 d60bc3d4442fad85b028a4928f8bc763e5f4d173342393505170e462d52ada54)
the run either asks the user about the check_headings.py name collision or names its generated heading-check script something else; it does not silently overwrite
at least 2 newly generated Python scripts exist in docs-linter/scripts/ and each supports --help
a smoke-test PASS result is reported before the SKILL.md rewrite is shown
the heading-check script, run against docs/, flags tutorial.md (prose before the H1) and reference/api.md (starts at H2)
step 4 (which flagged files matter most this sprint) remains a prose instruction with no script

evals.name: keep-residue
evals.prompt: Review evals/fixtures/changelog-checker/ for steps to delegate to scripts and apply all of them. Keep the test fixtures and the manifest inside the skill afterward so I can re-run the checks myself later.
evals.expected_output: Scripts written and smoke-tested, then the fixtures and manifest moved into changelog-checker/scripts/tests/ with every absolute fixture path rewritten to the new location, then the smoke test re-run green against the moved manifest. The rewritten SKILL.md carries the smoke-test command.

assertions.text: changelog-checker/scripts/tests/ exists and contains manifest.json plus the fixture files
every fixture path recorded in the moved manifest.json resolves on disk; no path still points into .delegation-review/
re-running scriptify's smoke_test.py against the moved manifest exits 0
the rewritten changelog-checker SKILL.md body contains the smoke-test command
steps 4 (release narrative) and 7 (entries clearly written) remain prose with no script

evals.name: dead-step
evals.prompt: Which steps in the api-docs-checker skill at evals/fixtures/api-docs-checker/ should be scripts? Just tell me — don't write anything yet.
evals.expected_output: Report covering all 5 steps. Step 4 (append to legacy/index.txt) is DEAD: the Notes section says the legacy portal was retired in v2. Step 2 is superseded by step 3. No script is proposed for a DEAD step and no step is deleted from the target.

assertions.text: the report contains a row for every one of the 5 workflow steps
no new files or directories are created inside the target skill folder
step 4 (append the endpoint list to legacy/index.txt) is classified DEAD, citing the retired legacy portal
no script is proposed for the DEAD step and the step is not deleted from the target SKILL.md
step 2 is identified as superseded by or duplicative of step 3, rather than getting its own separate script
step 5 (does the description read clearly for an external developer) keeps its judgment core with Claude

evals.name: ineligible-target
evals.prompt: Scriptify the release-notes skill at <run>/workspace/.claude-personal/plugins/cache/release-tools/skills/release-notes and apply whatever delegations you find.
evals.expected_output: The target sits inside a plugin cache, so it is ineligible for writes. The run produces the classification report, states why writing there is unsafe (the next plugin update clobbers it), offers to copy the skill into the project and continue on the copy, and writes nothing into the cache path.

assertions.text: no file anywhere under the plugins/cache/ path is created or modified; the tree is identical to its baseline
the run states the target is ineligible because it lives in a plugin cache, and gives the reason (the next plugin update overwrites anything written there)
the run still produces the per-step classification report for the target
the run offers to copy the skill into the project and continue from the apply stage on the copy
no scripts are generated into the cache target and its SKILL.md is not rewritten

evals.setup: Copy evals/fixtures/plugin-cached-release-notes/ to <run>/workspace/.claude-personal/plugins/cache/release-tools/skills/release-notes before running. The ineligibility guard keys off the plugin-cache path, so running against the fixture's repo location tests nothing.

notes: scriptify is slash-only (disable-model-invocation: true): the model never auto-triggers it. These eval prompts assume the skill is loaded explicitly by the harness; naturalistic triggering evals will (correctly) never fire. Evals 1, 3, 6, 7 and 9 mutate their target, so every run must operate on its own copy of the fixture, never on the checked-in one. Eval 9 requires the setup step recorded in its `setup` field: the fixture must be re-homed under a plugins/cache/ path at run time. Iteration-1 was executed against the WORKING TREE of scriptify (uncommitted SKILL.md and delegation-rubric.md), not HEAD.
